# Ensure that the proxy-usage-analysis is scripted as much as possible (LP-0MTY7CCQP002DOZ5)

## Headline

Retire the last LLM/agent step in the proxy-usage-analysis daily path: the
analysis pipeline is already fully deterministic (a ~5,200-line Python
script set) and the 05:00 cron already runs it unattended, so the remaining
work is to remove the herdr **scheduled-prompt** dispatch that puts an agent
in the daily loop and to reduce the skill definition to a thin, CLI-focused
wrapper around the script.

## Problem statement

The proxy-usage-analysis report is generated by a fully deterministic Python
pipeline, yet its daily cadence is still driven by an LLM agent: the herdr
downtime worker dispatches `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis --priority high`
once a day (LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM), which starts an agent whose only job is to
invoke the same script the 05:00 cron (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL) already runs.
The agent contributes no analysis of its own — the script produces the
report, the CSVs, and the recommendations — so the dispatch is redundant
overhead (agent tokens, an extra same-day archive like
`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-14_2/_3`, and a second code path to reason
about) with no operator-visible benefit. "Scripted as much as possible"
therefore means removing that last agent step, not re-scripting the
already-deterministic analysis.

## Users

- **rgardler (operator)** — wants the daily proxy-usage report produced
  hands-off by a non-interactive command, with no agent in the loop.
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I want the daily proxy report to be
    produced by a single scheduled script invocation (the 05:00 cron), so
    that the analysis is deterministic, cheap, and needs no agent or LLM to
    run."
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I still want to be able to run the
    analysis on demand via `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis` and have that
    simply invoke the CLI."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — Daily path is agent-free.** The daily proxy-usage report is
  produced solely by the existing 05:00 cron
  (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`),
  and `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` contains **no** `proxy-usage-analysis`
  entry — the LLM/agent dispatch (LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM) is retired. No other
  agent/LLM step remains in the daily path.
- [x] **AC2 — Agent-free path is verified and recorded.** A repeatable,
  documented check (e.g. `grep` over `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`,
  plus inspection of `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` and `crontab -l`)
  demonstrates that the cron is the sole trigger and no dispatch entry
  remains; the observed command + result is captured in a comment on this
  work item.
- [x] **AC3 — SKILL.md is a thin, CLI-focused wrapper.** The skill definition
  documents the non-interactive invocation and the 05:00 cron as the trigger,
  with agent-orchestration/imperative narration (e.g. the "EXECUTE
  immediately — do NOT ask permission or confirm" framing and any
  scheduler-dispatch references) removed. Substantive reference material that
  remains useful (report interpretation, root-cause taxonomy, limitations) is
  **retained or relocated to a linked doc**, not silently discarded.
- [x] **AC4 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- [x] **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **No change to the analysis itself.** The deterministic pipeline
  (`analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `aggregation.py`, `bucketing.py`,
  `recommendations.py`, `reporting.py`, `log_parser.py`, `llama_log_parser.py`)
  is out of scope; this item touches only the *invocation/cadence* and the
  *skill definition*.
- **No new code path.** The daily path must remain a single CLI invocation;
  do not add a wrapper script unless one is strictly required (the CLI
  already exists and the cron already calls it).
- **Runtime config, not committed.** `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` is a
  gitignored, per-project runtime config (absent ⇒ empty set, malformed ⇒
  empty set). Removing the entry is a local runtime edit, not a committed
  artifact.
- **Project-local only.** The skill exists only at
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (relocated from global by
  LP-0MSDFAFX0000SKQK); do not touch `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.
- **Preserve on-demand usability.** `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis` must
  continue to work as a manual, on-demand entry point to the CLI.
- **UK English** in all brief/docs prose.

## Existing state

- **Analysis pipeline — already fully scripted.** ~5,200 lines of
  deterministic Python behind `scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`, with a test
  suite under `tests/` (`test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `test_llama_log_parser.py`). Every report section — session summary,
  hourly busy table, total tokens, fallback reasons, error taxonomy,
  root-cause breakdown, compaction, TTFT, decode/prompt-eval speed,
  recommendations — is produced by rule-based code, not by an LLM.
- **Root-cause classification — already automated.** The one section
  previously described as a manual investigation was automated on
  2026-10-13 (LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS, LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T): `root_cause` is now
  a deterministic field in `errors.csv` / `errors.json` and the report's
  root-cause table.
- **Unattended cadence — already exists.** The 05:00 cron runs the script
  with output appended to `~/proxy-usage-reports/cron.log`, archiving each
  day's artifacts automatically (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL). Confirmed live in
  `crontab -l` and daily archives under `~/proxy-usage-reports/`.
- **The only agent step — the scheduled prompt.** `herdr`'s downtime worker
  dispatches `/skill:proxy-usage-analysis --priority high` once a day from
  `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (`lastTriggeredAt`
  2026-10-14T13:59:57.981Z). The dispatched agent's only action is to run the
  same script — hence the redundancy (evidenced by same-day archives such as
  `2026-10-14_2` and `2026-10-14_3`).
- **SKILL.md framing.** The skill is written as an agent-invoked slash
  command ("EXECUTE immediately via /skill:proxy-usage-analysis; do NOT ask
  permission or confirm") even though the substantive work is the CLI.

## Desired change

1. **Retire the agent dispatch (scope decision 1a).** Remove the
   `proxy-usage-analysis` entry from `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` so
   the herdr downtime worker no longer spawns an agent for the daily report.
2. **Confirm the cron is the sole daily trigger (definition of done 2a).**
   The existing 05:00 cron already yields "a single non-interactive command
   produces the daily report with no agent/LLM in the loop".
3. **Thin the skill definition.** Rewrite `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
   to a CLI-focused wrapper: non-interactive invocation + cron as the
   trigger; remove agent-orchestration narration; retain/relocate the
   substantive reference material (interpretation, taxonomy, limitations).

No new capability is added and no analysis behaviour changes — the change is
the removal of a redundant agent step plus the corresponding documentation
clean-up.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — Remove the `proxy-usage-analysis` entry
  (gitignored runtime config; local edit only).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — Reduce to a thin, CLI-focused
  wrapper; drop agent-orchestration/imperative narration; retain or relocate
  reference sections.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — Reference only (archives + `cron.log`) for AC2
  verification evidence; no edits.
- `crontab` (user crontab) — Reference only for AC2 verification; the cron
  entry is already present (LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL) and unchanged.

## Related work

### find-related report (automated)

The `/skill:find-related` scan returned three items by keyword overlap —
**LP-0MNWBTFDL009MJOS** (Logs Observability & Access), **LP-0MTVJF5HU007ISP1**
(Fix local summarizer timeout causing compaction failures), and
**LP-0MQR7AYXB006XPQ6** (Implementation roadmap & handoff) — all completed.
These are keyword-noise matches with no bearing on this item (they concern
log access, summariser timeouts, and a roadmap, not reporting cadence). Its
repository matches were likewise noise (large `ds4/.../rendered_prompts*.txt`
datasets). The meaningful related work is the curated list below.

### Curated related work items

- **LP-0MT2UKC26000D8YM** — Add project-local scheduled prompt for
  proxy-usage-analysis (completed). The dispatch being retired here.
- **LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL** — Archive proxy usage reports: auto-archive on each
  run + daily 05:00 cron (completed). The retained, agent-free mechanism.
- **LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS** / **LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T** — Classify stream-finish
  error root causes / adoption-aware stream-error recommendation and taxonomy
  (completed 2026-10-13). Automated the last previously-manual report
  section, making the pipeline fully deterministic.
- **LP-0MUIEO6IP0030CT3** — proxy-usage-analysis: exclude `chain_hold_cycle>0`
  re-emissions from local-skip demand counters (completed). Recent
  deterministic-analysis work.
- **LP-0MSDFAFX0000SKQK** — Relocate proxy-usage-analysis skill from global
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` to project-local `.pi/skills` (completed). Confirms
  the project-local-only constraint.
- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** — herdr scheduled-prompts feature (framework repo;
  not in this store). The mechanism whose entry is removed.
- **LP-0MTYARXXZ002VNF5**, **LP-0MTYAZFGN003BYQS**, **LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT** —
  Recent deterministic report extensions (log discovery, hourly bucketing,
  compaction reporting); evidence the pipeline is scripted.

## Risks

- **Documentation loss.** "Thin wrapper" could drop genuinely useful
  reference prose (root-cause taxonomy, limitations, interpretation guide).
  *Mitigation:* AC3 requires retention/relocation, not silent deletion.
- **Loss of the agent-curated summary.** Scope (1a) explicitly accepts that
  the daily report is the raw script output; no LLM narrative is produced.
  *Mitigation:* accepted by producer decision; the script's stdout summary +
  `report.md` remain.
- **Silent cron failure.** Without the daily agent as a second caller, a cron
  failure would go unnoticed. *Mitigation:* out of scope here — note as
  linked follow-up if desired (`cron.log` already records failures).
- **Scope creep.** Securing the agent-free path could tempt further pipeline
  changes. *Mitigation:* constraints confine the change to invocation +
  skill docs.
- **Idempotence of the runtime edit.** A re-run must not fail on an already
  absent entry. *Mitigation:* removal is a no-op when absent.

## Assumptions

- The 05:00 cron remains the intended daily mechanism (confirmed via
  `crontab -l` and LP-0MSI8W67N007RJIL).
- The scheduled-prompt entry is no longer wanted for this skill
  (producer decision 1a).
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/cron.log` remains the operational failure record.
- No CI/CD pipeline test changes are required (per intake guidance, CI/CD
  pipeline tests are excluded).
- The work-item title retains the original spelling "proxy-useage-analysis"
  (as authored); the brief uses the corrected term "proxy-usage-analysis".

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Round 1 — 2026-09-26 (original intake attempt; unanswered at the time)

- Q (2026-09-26): "Scope — what still counts as 'not scripted'? (a) replace
  the LLM-driven daily invocation with a direct non-interactive script/cron
  call; (b) accept as already scripted and close; (c) automate remaining
  manual sections (e.g. root-cause classification)." — **Answer: deferred**
  (no answer recorded during the first session). Context: option (c) was
  independently delivered on 2026-10-13 (LP-0MUQO82LJ008F1FS /
  LP-0MUQO862C004UT7T). Re-asked as Q1 in Round 2.
- Q (2026-09-26): "Definition of done — what observable outcome proves
  'scripted as much as possible'?" — **Answer: deferred.** Re-asked as Q2 in
  Round 2.
- Q (2026-09-26): "Trigger/context — what prompted this item now? Any case
  where the LLM-driven invocation produced inconsistent/incomplete output
  versus the 05:00 cron?" — **Answer: deferred.** Re-asked as Q3 in Round 2.

### Round 2 — 2026-10-14 (producer answered)

- Q1: "Scope: (a) retire the LLM-in-the-loop daily dispatch (rely on the
  05:00 cron only, remove the `proxy-usage-analysis` entry from
  `scheduled-prompts.json`, thin SKILL.md); (b) accept current state and
  close; (c) script a specific remaining step?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-14): (a).** Source: interactive reply. Research: verified the
  pipeline is deterministic and the root-cause taxonomy was automated
  2026-10-13, leaving the scheduled-prompt dispatch as the only agent step.
- Q2: "Definition of done: (a) a single non-interactive command (the
  existing CLI via cron) produces the daily report; no agent/LLM in the loop;
  `scheduled-prompts.json` no longer contains the entry; SKILL.md documents
  only the CLI with no agent-narration steps; (b) keep the scheduled prompt
  and add an audit checklist?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): (a).**
  Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Trigger: (a) a specific incident where the LLM-driven invocation
  produced inconsistent/incomplete output versus the 05:00 cron; (b) general
  hygiene — no specific incident?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14): (b),
  general hygiene.** Source: interactive reply. Evidence for the underlying
  redundancy: same-day duplicate archives (`2026-10-14_2`, `2026-10-14_3`
  under `~/proxy-usage-reports/`).

# Intake — ruff I001 at `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503` (candidate false positive)

## Goal

Decide whether the audit-generated "candidate false positive" tracking chore for
ruff `I001` at `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503` needs any action, and close
it as stale if the finding is already resolved.

## Problem statement

An automated code-quality scan (audit) raised ruff `I001` (import block
un-sorted) at `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503` and — because it was
classified as a medium/low "confident false positive" — created this tracking
chore for a producer decision (audit policy does not auto-remediate non-blocking
findings). The underlying finding has since been remediated by
`LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221` (commit `3cf3616a`), and `ruff check .` passes at current
HEAD. The chore is therefore stale, and its suggested fix is now
counterproductive.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer.** Needs to confirm the finding is resolved and close
  the stale chore without spending an implementation cycle.
  - "As a producer, I want to know whether the I001 finding still exists at HEAD
    so I can close the tracking chore if it does not."
  - "As a ruff-config maintainer, I want a standing decision on whether `proxy`
    should be declared first-party (`known-first-party`), so future import-block
    findings are classified consistently."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The producer decision is recorded on the work item: either **(a)** close as
  stale/superseded (recommended — no code or config change), or **(b)** adopt the
  first-party config route (AC3). Metric: a decision comment naming option (a) or
  (b).
- [ ] `ruff check .` at the revision used for closure reports zero `I001`
  findings; the exact command and output are captured on the work item. (Already
  true at HEAD `1e730609`.)
- [ ] If option (b) is chosen: `.ruff.toml` declares
  `known-first-party = ["proxy"]`, the affected import blocks use
  blank-line-separated third-party/first-party grouping, and `ruff check .`
  passes.
- [ ] The duplicate open chore `LP-0MUHVTU67008BJ5N` (same finding) is
  reconciled — closed as a duplicate or explicitly linked. Metric: linked item
  reference or closed status.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Evidence (current state)

- `ruff check .` at HEAD (`1e730609`) → `All checks passed!`;
  `ruff check proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py --select I001` → passes.
- The original finding item `LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221` (completed, `in_review`) fixed
  the finding in commit `3cf3616a`: it moved
  `from starlette.responses import JSONResponse` below the three
  `import proxy.*` lines, collapsing the blank-line-separated block that
  triggered `I001`.
- The chore's suggested `known-first-party = ["proxy"]` fix is
  **counterproductive at HEAD**: under the current single-section block, that
  setting raises **14** `I001` findings across the file (verified with
  `ruff --config 'lint.isort.known-first-party = ["proxy"]'`), because it then
  requires a blank line between third-party `starlette` and first-party `proxy`.
- A duplicate open tracking chore exists: `LP-0MUHVTU67008BJ5N` (identical
  finding, already `needsProducerReview: true`).

## Constraints

- **Severity policy:** medium/low findings are never auto-remediated by the
  audit; any action requires an explicit producer decision.
- **Repo-wide config blast radius:** changing `known-first-party` in `.ruff.toml`
  affects import classification for every Python file, not just this one.
- **Repository boundaries:** do not edit `.pi/` or `skill/` trees; this chore
  lives in the `llm` repo.
- **No behaviour change:** any accepted change must be purely cosmetic (import
  ordering / lint config).

## Existing state

The import block at `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py:503` is already sorted
under the current `.ruff.toml` (no `known-first-party`). The finding no longer
reproduces.

## Desired change

No code change is recommended. The desired outcome is a producer decision to
close this stale tracking chore (and its duplicate), optionally recording the
`known-first-party` policy choice for future audits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py` — import block at line ~503; already sorted
  at HEAD (fixed by `3cf3616a`).
- `.ruff.toml` — ruff config; only touched under option (b) to add
  `known-first-party`.
- `README.md` — "Python linting" section (~lines 117-156); update only if the
  config changes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — acting on a stale finding:** applying the chore's suggested fix at
  HEAD would introduce 14 new `I001` findings and dirty the config for no
  benefit. Mitigation: treat this as a closure decision, not an implementation
  task; re-verify `ruff check .` before any change.
- **Risk — duplicate churn:** a second open chore
  (`LP-0MUHVTU67008BJ5N`) covers the same finding; both could be actioned
  independently. Mitigation: reconcile the pair in one decision.
- **Risk — scope creep into lint-policy redesign:** the `known-first-party`
  question affects import classification repo-wide. Mitigation: keep it out of
  scope unless the producer explicitly selects option (b); record any broader
  lint-policy work as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the audit's false-positive classification referred to the
  pre-`3cf3616a` block (blank line between `starlette` and `proxy`), which no
  longer exists at HEAD.
- **Assumption:** no other `I001` findings exist repo-wide at HEAD (verified:
  `ruff check .` passes).

## Related work

- `LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221` (completed, `in_review`) — original I001 code-quality
  fix; commit `3cf3616a` resolved this finding.
- `LP-0MUHVTU67008BJ5N` (open, `needsProducerReview`) — duplicate tracking chore
  for the same finding.
- `LP-0MSXZ06M5007CPN6`, `LP-0MSXZ072M0085AF5`, `LP-0MSXZ07AP000EBO7`
  (completed) — precedent ruff false-positive/config chores.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (RESOLVED, 2026-10-14):** Decision recorded on the work item as **option (a) — close as stale/superseded** (no code or config change). Verified at HEAD `9f094720`: `ruff check .` and `ruff check proxy/tests/test_startup_ramp.py --select I001` both pass (zero I001); the finding was fixed by `LP-0MUBDKDFG002W221` (commit `3cf3616a`). Option (b) (`known-first-party = ["proxy"]`) deliberately rejected: it introduces 14 I001 findings at HEAD. Duplicate `LP-0MUHVTU67008BJ5N` already deleted. `needsProducerReview` retained for producer ratification before release.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **LP-0MSXZ06M5007CPN6** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:10 — Expected a statement (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ072M0085AF5** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:12 — Expected `,`, found name (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ07AP000EBO7** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:12 — Expected `,`, found int (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: already, block, candidate, code, config (+24 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: already, block, candidate, code, config (+24 more)

# Objective

De-duplicate the `proxy-usage-analysis` local-skip / demand counters by
parsing `chain_hold_cycle` and excluding `chain_hold_cycle > 0` re-emissions
from the demand aggregates, while surfacing them separately as hold-cycle
re-emission activity.

## Problem statement

LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0 added a `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` field to the proxy's
`routing_check` / `routing_skip_local` / `compaction_bypass_eval` /
hold-start log lines so a single held request re-emitted across chain-hold
cycles is distinguishable from genuine new client demand. The
`proxy-usage-analysis` consumer has not been updated: `aggregation.py`
increments `hourly_activity[hour]['local_skip']` (and appends to
`routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`, and
`routing_skip_reason_counts`) for **every** `routing_skip` event, so a held
request that re-emits its skip once per cycle (up to `chain_hold_max_cycles`)
is counted N+1 times — inflating the local-skip / demand counters and making
one held request read as repeated client retries.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / agent analyst** reading the daily `proxy-usage-analysis`
  report: needs the "Local-skip" numbers and the
  `## routing_skip_local reasons` table to reflect genuine client demand, not
  chain-hold re-emissions.
- **Downstream JSON consumer** (dashboard / automated agent) querying
  `summary_to_json()` per-hour activity: needs the same de-duplication, plus a
  way to see hold-cycle re-emission volume separately.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when a session is held through N chain-hold cycles, I want
  its local-skip counted once so my fallback/demand ratios are accurate.
- As an operator, I want to see that a request was re-emitted N times by the
  hold cycle (separately from demand) so I can tell a stuck hold from a client
  retry storm.

## Existing state

- Producer side (shipped, LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0): `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  emits `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` on the `routing_check`, `routing_skip_local`,
  and `compaction_bypass_eval` INFO lines and on the hold-start WARNING line.
  Cycle 0 is the first (pre-hold) cycle; every hold-restart increments it.
- Consumer side (unchanged): `log_parser.py` recognises only
  `routing_skip_local` among those lines and does not parse
  `chain_hold_cycle`; `aggregation.aggregate` counts every `routing_skip`
  event identically, regardless of cycle.
- The existing `ROUTING_SKIP_*` test fixtures predate the field (no
  `chain_hold_cycle` token), so pre-chain-hold log lines must keep parsing.

## Desired change

- Parse `chain_hold_cycle=<N>` in `log_parser.py` into a new
  `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle: int | None` field (tolerant: absent → `None`).
- In `aggregation.py`, exclude `routing_skip` events with
  `chain_hold_cycle > 0` from the demand / local-skip counters and aggregates,
  while recording them separately as hold-cycle re-emission activity.
- Surface the separate hold-cycle activity in the report/JSON.
- Add parser/aggregation/reporting tests covering a held request across
  cycles, plus a backward-compatibility test for logs without the field.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `log_parser.parse_log_line` populates `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle` with the
   integer parsed from `chain_hold_cycle=N` on a `routing_skip_local` line, and
   leaves it `None` when the token is absent (pre-chain-hold log lines).
   Verified by parser unit tests using new fixtures with and without the token.
2. `aggregation.aggregate` counts a single held request re-emitted across
   cycles exactly once in `hourly_activity[...]['local_skip']`,
   `routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`, and
   `routing_skip_reason_counts` (the cycle-0 occurrence), while the new
   hold-cycle re-emission activity (`hold_cycle_routing_skip_events` and its
   count) reflects the `chain_hold_cycle > 0` occurrences. Verified by an
   aggregation test feeding one cycle-0 and three cycle>0 events for the same
   session.
3. The operator report and `summary_to_json()` surface the hold-cycle
   re-emission activity as its own metric and exclude it from the
   `routing_skip_local reasons` counts and the local-skip percentage
   denominators. Verified by a reporting test.
4. Backward compatibility: log lines without `chain_hold_cycle` (older rotated
   logs) are treated as cycle 0, so all pre-existing routing-skip tests and
   aggregates are unchanged. Verified by the existing suite plus a new
   explicit no-field test.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `SKILL.md`, and any relevant docs-site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary (recorded exception):** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`
  is agent-infrastructure, normally off-limits per AGENTS.md; this work item
  explicitly authorises changes confined to that skill's `scripts/` and
  `tests/` (and its `SKILL.md`). No other agent-infrastructure directories are
  touched.
- **No proxy-side changes:** the log field is already produced by
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py`; this task is consumer-only.
- Parsing must remain tolerant/unfatal: a missing or malformed
  `chain_hold_cycle` must never drop a line (default to `None`/cycle 0).

## Assumptions (documented; no operator response required)

- **A1 — absent field = cycle 0.** Pre-chain-hold log lines and any line
  missing the token are treated as genuine demand (cycle 0). This preserves
  historic counts and avoids silently discarding real skips.
- **A2 — exclude from counters, surface separately.** `chain_hold_cycle > 0`
  events are removed from every demand/local-skip aggregate (hourly
  `local_skip`, `routing_skip_events`, per-session `routing_skips`,
  `routing_skip_reason_counts`, and the report reasons table/percentages) and
  recorded instead in a dedicated hold-cycle re-emission list/counter. This is
  the union of the item's "exclude (or flag)" wording and matches the stated
  intent of "still surfacing them as hold-cycle activity".
- **A3 — scope limited to parsed `routing_skip` events.** `routing_check` and
  `compaction_bypass_eval` are not parsed today and feed no counters; parsing
  them (and adding demand counters over `routing_check`) is out of scope to
  avoid scope creep. The new `LogEvent` field is nonetheless generic so a
  future parser addition can reuse it.
- **A4 — the "demand counter" is the local-skip activity.** The only
  re-emitted event that reaches a counter is `routing_skip_local`;
  `stream_started`/`requests_started` is not re-emitted by hold cycles, so it
  is already unaffected. "demand counters" in the title is read as the
  counters that proxy genuine demand (local-skip).

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — add
  `RE_CHAIN_HOLD_CYCLE`, the `LogEvent.chain_hold_cycle` field, and populate it
  when parsing `routing_skip_local` (docs/comments updated).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — split
  `routing_skip` handling on `chain_hold_cycle > 0`; new
  `AnalysisResult.hold_cycle_routing_skip_events` and a
  `hold_cycle_reemission_count` property; keep cycle-0 events in existing
  aggregates.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — surface hold-cycle
  re-emissions separately (report line/section + `summary_to_json()` field)
  and ensure the reasons table/percentages use only genuine skips.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — add `routing_skip_local`
  fixtures with `chain_hold_cycle=0` and `>0`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — parser,
  aggregation, reporting, and backward-compatibility tests.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — document the field and the
  demand-vs-re-emission distinction.

## Related work

- Parent discovery: **LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0** — "Chain-hold cycles re-run
  provider resolution but never re-run session handling / compaction"
  (completed; shipped the `chain_hold_cycle` log field).
- Epic: **LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO** — "Overnight remote-chain exhaustion: accurate
  diagnostics, quarantine visibility, bounded chain-hold" (open) — explicitly
  calls out the downstream observability requirement this item implements.
- Producer code: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_log_chain_hold_start`,
  `routing_check`, `routing_skip_local`, `compaction_bypass_eval`).
- Consumer code: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/{log_parser,aggregation,reporting}.py`.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Report count drop is intended but visible.** Local-skip totals fall for
  windows containing held requests; document in the report/SKILL.md so the
  change is not mistaken for lost data.
- **Over-exclusion risk.** If a genuine new request ever carried
  `chain_hold_cycle > 0` it would be dropped; cycle is per-request state set
  by `_set_chain_hold_cycle`, so this cannot occur — covered by an aggregation
  test asserting cycle 0 is retained.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Parsing `routing_check` / `compaction_bypass_eval` or
  adding new demand counters is tempting; recorded here as out of scope
  (A3) and to be raised as a separate work item if needed.
- **Backward-compat risk.** Malformed/absent field must not crash or drop the
  line; covered by the tolerant-parse + no-field tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking clarifying questions were raised during this intake — the seed
context (problem, change, references) was sufficient to draft a testable
brief. The following non-blocking design choices were resolved by the agent
with documented assumptions (see Assumptions A1–A4); the operator may override
any of them at review:

- Q: Exclude or flag `chain_hold_cycle > 0` events? — **Resolved: exclude from
  demand/local-skip counters, surface separately** (A2). Source: this intake's
  documented assumption, consistent with the item's "exclude (or flag) …
  while still surfacing them as hold-cycle activity".
- Q: Treat an absent `chain_hold_cycle` as demand? — **Resolved: yes, cycle 0**
  (A1). Source: documented assumption preserving historic counts.
- Q: Extend to `routing_check` / `compaction_bypass_eval`? — **Resolved: no**
  (A3), out of scope. Source: documented assumption; they feed no counters.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTJET4R5002U1FW** – Test: Contented queue invariants regression (completed)
- **LP-0MR4ZIGDT004A3E1** – Show the model being used in Pi (completed)

# Raise Qwen3 cache-ram to 40,960 MiB

Follow-up to LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW (which verified the 32,768 MiB cap on the
live post-deploy window) and LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN.

## Context

The 2026-10-12 post-32-GiB verification
(`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) showed the cache is
still saturating under the current single-slot load:

- 18 evictions over ~4.7 d (1.28% of requests; 65 -> 18 vs the length-matched
  8 GiB window, a 72.9%/req reduction);
- 26.3% of cache-state samples above 90% of the 32,768 MiB cap (vs 22.0% at
  8 GiB);
- observed maximum 16 concurrently-retained prompts, cache peak 32,765.6 MiB
  (fully saturated).

`scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py --recommend` over that measurement derives
**40,960 MiB (40 GiB)**:

    per-prompt state 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25 margin = 40,260 MiB
    -> round up to 40,960 MiB (holds ~20 prompts >= observed 16)

Headroom is safe (host available 79,248 MiB - 40,960 = 38,288 MiB, well above
the 12,743.7 MiB reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)), so the
`server_prompt_cache::alloc()` OOM fallback (`limit_size = 0.4 * size()`) is
not approached.

## Goal

As a proxy operator, raise the Qwen3 prompt-cache cap to the derived
40,960 MiB so the cache stops saturating and evicting session prefixes under
the single-slot load, with the derivation and headroom recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` raised 32768 -> 40960, with the
   derivation (per-prompt 2,013 MiB x observed max 16 x 1.25) and the
   2026-10-12 measurement reference recorded in the comment block.
2. Headroom invariant re-checked at 40,960 MiB: MemAvailable - 40960 >= reserve
   (reserve = max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)); the OOM fallback path is documented
   as avoided.
3. Deploy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never kill the proxy manually);
   confirm the spawned Qwen3 child carries `--cache-ram 40960` (and
   `--ctx-checkpoints 32`, no `--swa-full`).
4. `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` updated with the new cap, the derivation
   and the deploy evidence.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Non-goals

- Changing `ctx-checkpoints` / `checkpoint-every-n-tokens` (kept at 32; the
  checkpoint term is not the lever, see `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md`).
- Re-tuning routing cold/warm thresholds.
- The live post-deploy validation of this change (separate follow-up).

Discovered from: LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW

# Wire proxy/prompts/author.txt into the author model system_prompt config

## Problem statement

The `author` model alias in `proxy/config.yaml` has no `system_prompt` block, so the wiki authoring guidelines in `proxy/prompts/author.txt` (116 lines, including the "explain names on first mention" rule from LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) are never loaded by the proxy. No client supplies the content client-side, so the prompt currently has zero effect — the completed LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE deliverable is unreachable through the proxy's auto-loading path.

## Users

- **Wiki authoring operators** invoking the `author` alias (directly or via an authoring client) — they expect the mandatory wiki guidelines to shape every `author` response.
- **Readers of the open_source_llm wiki** — indirectly benefit from consistent openness terminology, citation, and naming conventions.

Example user stories:

- As an operator authoring wiki content via the `author` alias, I want the proxy to inject `proxy/prompts/author.txt` into my requests so that terminology/openness classification and citation rules are applied without me having to paste the guidelines each time.
- As a wiki reader, I want model categories consistently labelled (open-source vs open-weights vs closed) and project/concept names explained at first mention (LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE) so pages are accurate and navigable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `proxy/config.yaml` gains a `system_prompt` block on the `author` entry with `mode: "override"` and `file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"`, and config validation passes at load time.
- [ ] A test asserts `resolve_system_prompt("author", model_cfg)` against the real config returns the author.txt content (mode `override`, correct `source` path); an injection-path test asserts an `author` request's system messages are replaced by author.txt content (mode `override`).
- [ ] The proxy auto-loading path is verified live: a `model=author` request through `proxy_openai_api` applies the resolved prompt (first real-world use of the `system_prompt` feature).
- [ ] Documentation is updated to reflect the wiring, including `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (author as a worked `system_prompt` example) and code comments as needed.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (build → test → commit order).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Keep the `system_prompt` schema as documented in `proxy/config.yaml` (lines 113–127): optional block, `mode` ∈ {override, prepend} (required), `file` relative to repo root.
- Resolution precedence must be preserved: local override (`.sorraAgents/prompts/author.txt`, currently absent) → repo default (`proxy/prompts/author.txt`).
- `author.txt` must stay within the resolver's max file size (64 KB); content changes are out of scope here (author.txt content is owned by LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE / prompt-content work).
- No changes to the resolver or request-handling code unless a defect is found while wiring; prefer configuration-only change.

## Existing state

- `proxy/config.yaml` author entry (lines 334–408) has providers only; no `system_prompt` block.
- `resolve_system_prompt()` (`proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py:82`) returns `None` when `model_cfg["system_prompt"]` is absent.
- `proxy_openai_api` (`proxy/proxy/ui.py:1254`) is the live injection point for `/v1/chat/completions`; `compose_messages` applies override/prepend.
- No model entry in `config.yaml` currently has an active `system_prompt` block — author becomes the first live use.
- No client in `~/projects`, `~/.pi`, or the open_source_llm tooling references author.txt or its content; only `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py:436` reads it.

## Desired change

1. Add the `system_prompt` block to the `author` entry in `proxy/config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   author:
     providers:
       # ... existing providers unchanged ...
     system_prompt:
       mode: "override"   # operator-confirmed; replaces client system messages
       file: "proxy/prompts/author.txt"
   ```

2. Add tests: real-config resolution for `author` → author.txt (mode `override`), plus an injection-path assertion that an `author` request's system messages are replaced.
3. Document the wiring in `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (worked example) and any code comments.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml` — Add `system_prompt` block to the `author` entry (lines 334–408).
- `proxy/proxy/prompt_resolver.py` — Reference only; no change expected (resolution + precedence already implemented).
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — Reference only; `proxy_openai_api` already applies resolved prompts (no change expected).
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_resolution.py` — Add test asserting `resolve_system_prompt("author", model_cfg)` returns author.txt with mode `override`.
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_injection_integration.py` — Add/extend test asserting `author` requests get system messages replaced (mode `override`).
- `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — Document author as the worked `system_prompt` example.
- `proxy/README.md` — Update if it lists per-model features.

## Related work

- `Add 'explain project and concept names at first use' rule to the author system prompt (LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE)` — completed; discoverer. Its deliverable lives in author.txt but is currently unreachable; this task makes it effective.
- `Assign custom system prompts to model aliases (LP-0MNXBI97B00773WF)` — completed; introduced the `system_prompt` config feature.
- `Config schema & validation (LP-0MPXTZ71W0024ISW)` — completed; schema + validation for `system_prompt`.
- `Prompt resolver (LP-0MPXTZAG0001BMHU)` — completed; implemented `resolve_system_prompt`.
- `Prompt resolution tests (LP-0MPXTYWL70047KKD)` — completed; base test coverage for resolution.
- `Config: plan and code aliases (LP-0MQ5BMWO1001HRLV)` — completed; noted `system_prompt` blocks could be added per alias later (this task does exactly that for author).
- `Add author fallback model with same fallback chain as plan (LP-0MRPDJ2XF005Y9XN)` — completed; predecessor author wiring.
- `Binding registry and restricted-model detection (LP-0MSMFQ8SU003PJV9)` — completed; surfaced by find-related, moderate relevance (alias↔model binding machinery adjacent to config wiring).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — override is destructive:** `mode: "override"` replaces *all* system messages for `author` requests, including any client-supplied system prompt. Assumption (operator-confirmed): the author client sends no needed client-side system prompt, and author.txt is intended as the complete system prompt for authoring. Mitigation: document this in MODEL_ADD.md and note the local-override escape hatch (`.sorraAgents/prompts/author.txt`) for per-deployment overrides.
- **Assumption:** no client currently injects author.txt content client-side — verified by repo-wide search; if a client later sends its own copy, precedence/duplication should be revisited.
- **Assumption:** no resolver/handler code changes are needed; if wiring reveals a defect, scope a follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Scope-creep guard:** author.txt *content* changes (rules, wording) are already owned by LP-0MUYJHQ2W002I0CE and out of scope here; this task is wiring + tests + docs only.

## Open questions (resolved)

- **Original open question** (from description): does the wiki authoring client already send author.txt as a client-supplied system message? — **Resolved:** no client reference found anywhere; proxy auto-load is the correct path (operator confirm + repo search).
- **Mode override vs prepend** — **Resolved by operator: `override`.**

# Don't truncate session ID in the log

## Problem statement

On the `/logs` Web UI page, the slot session badge truncates session IDs to 8 characters (e.g. `11111111…`) in the slot header. The full session ID is available only via hover tooltip, making it hard to copy or correlate at a glance. The session dropdown and slot `data-session` attribute already carry the full ID.

## Users

- **LLM operators / proxy team** — Monitor concurrent slots on the `/logs` page and need to see or copy full session IDs without hovering.
- **Map (agent/auditor)** — Correlating slot logs to specific sessions via the Web UI.

## Existing state

- **Key file:** `proxy/templates/view_logs.html`
  - `shortSession()` (line 1049) truncates to 8 chars for IDs longer than 24 chars: `sessionId.substring(0, 8) + '…'`
  - Called from `buildSlotSection()` (line 1067) and `updateSlotHeader()` (line 1193)
  - Full ID is already available: `title` attribute on `<span class="slot-session">`, `data-session` attribute on `.slot-section`, and `dataset.sessionId`
- **Test:** `proxy/tests/slot-logs.spec.js:106` asserts `toContainText(SESSION_A.substring(0, 8))`
- **Related:** `proxy/templates/index.html` truncates session IDs to 16 chars on the home page (out of scope — separate concern)
- **Precedent:** LP-0MT1TGQC1002X5RH (completed) removed `[:8]` truncation from backend lease/orphan log events

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** The slot session badge on the `/logs` page (`view_logs.html`) displays the full session ID — no truncation or ellipsis.
2. **AC2:** The slot header layout remains readable (the session badge must not overflow or break the header row).
3. **AC3:** The Playwright test (`slot-logs.spec.js`) asserts the full session ID (not the truncated prefix) and passes.
4. **AC4:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **AC5:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Minimal change — touch only `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` (remove `shortSession()` truncation) and its test.
- The `.slot-session` CSS class (`font-size:0.8rem; color:var(--text-secondary); font-family:monospace;`) should accommodate the full ID without breaking the header flex layout.
- No backend changes required — the full ID is already available in the SSE payload.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — Remove `shortSession()` truncation in `buildSlotSection()` and `updateSlotHeader()`
- `proxy/tests/slot-logs.spec.js` — Update assertion from truncated prefix to full session ID

## Scope notes

- **In scope:** `/logs` page slot session badge only.
- **Out of scope:** Home page (`index.html`) which also truncates session IDs to 16 chars — this is a separate concern that can be addressed in a follow-up if desired.

## Related work

- **LP-0MT1TGQC1002X5RH** — "Log full session IDs in lease/orphan events (remove [:8] truncation)" — backend precedent for full IDs
- **LP-0MSHET5SI000LYSK** — "Web UI logs interface that shows the current logs for each active slot" — built the slot log page we are modifying
- **LP-0MSU9RL07004FVGO** — Parent audit of lease timeout change (where LP-0MT1TGQC1002X5RH was discovered)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: layout overflow** — Full session IDs (~36 chars for UUIDs) may be wider than 8 chars. Mitigation: CSS `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, or `white-space: nowrap` on `.slot-session` if needed.
- **Risk: test assertion mismatch** — `slot-logs.spec.js` asserts truncated prefix; `toContainText` will still match since full text contains the prefix, but the test should be updated to assert the full ID.
- **Assumption:** No CSS changes are needed to maintain layout — the session badge has sufficient space in the header flex row. If layout is affected, add `max-width` + `overflow: hidden` to `.slot-session`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions

No clarifying questions — the seed context (work-item title and description) was sufficient.

# Fix accidentally committed broken proxy/node_modules symlink (re-introduced)

## Problem statement

The repository tracks `proxy/node_modules` as a broken self-referential git symlink (`proxy/node_modules → /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/node_modules`), which breaks `npm install` and Playwright runs inside `proxy/`. The symlink was previously removed in LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT (commit a45bb99f) with a .gitignore hardening, but was re-introduced by commit b6c238ed.

## Users

- **LLM operators / proxy developers** — Cannot run `npm install` or Playwright tests in `proxy/` without a manual workaround.
- **Map (agent/auditor)** — Automated tooling fails when operating in `proxy/`.

## Existing state

- `proxy/node_modules` is tracked as mode 120000 (symlink) pointing to itself — a broken loop.
- `proxy/.gitignore` was hardened in a45bb99f to ignore `node_modules` (symlink form), but the symlink was re-committed in b6c238ed.
- Root cause: the implement framework's `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` auto-symlinks `node_modules` from the main checkout into worktrees; if the symlink lands in a commit, the .gitignore pattern does not prevent it from being tracked (git adds what's staged, regardless of .gitignore).
- A related framework concern was noted in LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT's closing comment.

## Desired change

Remove `proxy/node_modules` from git tracking and prevent recurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `git ls-files | grep node_modules` returns no results — no `node_modules` entries tracked in any branch.
2. **AC2:** `proxy/node_modules` does not appear in `git status` after any `implement.py start` / `implement.py finish` cycle.
3. **AC3:** `npm install` can run successfully in `proxy/` without pre-existing symlinks or workarounds.
4. **AC4:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **AC5:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The implement framework's `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` mechanism must not re-introduce tracked symlinks.
- Solution must work across all branches (not just `dev`).
- Avoid broad `.gitignore` changes that might affect other legitimate symlink tracking.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/.gitignore` — May need further hardening to cover edge cases.
- `scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — The `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` function may need to exclude symlinks from staging.
- `.gitignore` (main checkout) — Consider adding `proxy/node_modules` at the repo root level.
- `proxy/package.json` — Verify `npm install` works post-fix.

## Related work

- **LP-0MUIH7FYS0010MLT** — "Remove accidentally committed proxy/node_modules symlink; harden gitignore" (completed, a45bb99f) — previously removed this symlink and hardened `proxy/.gitignore`, but it was re-introduced.
- **LP-0MUIEK47X000WL2C** — "Migrate proxy/scripts consumers to shared log helper" (commit 91b78adf) — first re-introduction.
- **LP-0MUI56OCI008EGML** — "Split Time to first token by cheap/fast" (commit b6c238ed) — second re-introduction (latest).
- **LP-0MTCZ35X7009IZKE** — "Remove local_max_concurrent_queries legacy key + add lease label to WebUI slot status" (commit 7d9a24f1) — original introduction.
- **LP-0MV6CZGN6003Z5QI** — "Don't truncate session ID in the log" — discovered this symlink issue during implementation.

- **Risk: implement framework re-creates symlink** — The root cause is the framework's auto-symlink mechanism. # Implement grace-period immunity: local cold-start 503s must not trigger a 60s local cooldown

## Problem statement

After a proxy restart, local (Qwen3) requests that race llama-server warm-up receive HTTP 503 and are treated identically to genuine failures — applying the standard `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` quarantine and feeding the failure counter. This causes the dominant source of ~60s local quarantines (~12 of 45 episodes in one 24h window), even though the 503 reflects "not ready yet" rather than a provider fault.

## Users

- **Local-proxy operator:** wants the proxy to recover immediately after a restart without wasting up to 60s of requests per restart.
- **Pi-extension / end-user:** experiences dropped requests or latency spikes during restarts.

## User stories

- As a proxy operator, when llama-server is cold after a restart, a local request that receives HTTP 503 should defer (Retry-After) without quarantining the provider.
- As a proxy operator, when local continues to return HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window, the standard cooldown should still apply (genuine faults not masked).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A deterministic unit test reproduces the current cold-start 503 → 60s cooldown, then verifies it no longer occurs after the change.
2. Tests cover:
   - (a) Cold-start 503 within the `is_cold()` warm-up window → defer via Retry-After, no cooldown, no failure-counter bump.
   - (b) Sustained HTTP 503 **after** the warm-up window ends → normal cooldown applies.
   - (c) Connection error during warm-up → defer, no cooldown.
   - (d) Concurrent cold-start dispatch gating (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`) still respected.
   - (e) A fresh warm-up window begins after each restart (new `note_model_loaded()` arms it).
3. The exponential-backoff failure counter is not polluted during the warm-up window.
4. No regression in routing/fallback tests; full suite passes via `/skill:test` before commit.
5. Follows the implement workflow (worktree, build → test → commit).
6. Logs/metrics evidence pre/post: local cooldown episodes in the hour after a restart drop to ~0.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments in `cold_start.py`/`provider.py`, `proxy/config.yaml` knobs, and any relevant docs entries (e.g. `proxy/docs/`).

## Constraints

- **Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal.** No new window plumbing. The existing grace window already bounds the immunity period and is self-expiring.
- **Only HTTP 503 + connection errors defer during the window.** All other 5xx during warm-up still quarantine — a genuine sustained non-503 fault is still quarantined.
- **Behaviour applies per restart event.** A new `note_model_loaded()` call arms a fresh warm-up window.
- **Must interact correctly with existing concurrent cold-start dispatch gating** (`local_cold_start_max_concurrent`).
- **No magic sleeps.** The readiness/warm-up signal is explicit and bounded.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking genuine local faults.** Mitigated by deferring only HTTP 503 + connection errors, and only while `is_cold()` is True — any other 5xx or post-window 503 still quarantines.
- **Risk: window not armed when 503s arrive.** If some warm-up 503s occur before `note_model_loaded()` arms the window, immunity will not cover them; verifiable in tests/logs, and if a gap exists it becomes a follow-up (not in scope here).
- **Risk: deferral storm.** Deferring during cold-start must respect the existing `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` gating so a burst of deferred requests does not accumulate unboundedly.
- **Assumption:** `is_cold()` semantics (armed at model load, self-expiring grace window) are the correct boundary; per Q1 this was confirmed by the operator.
- **Scope creep guard:** extending immunity to other status codes, other providers, or re-architecting the cold-start state machine is **out of scope** — record as separate work items if discovered.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — manages a bounded cold-start grace window: `note_model_loaded()`, `mark_warm()`, `is_cold()`, `note_backend_down()`. Config: `local_cold_start_grace_seconds` (default 120), `local_cold_start_max_concurrent` (default 1), `local_cold_start_retry_after_seconds` (default 15).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (line ~4871) calls `mark_provider_unavailable()` for all HTTP errors including 503; `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (line ~4832) does the same for connection errors. Exponential backoff only applies to remote providers.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — denies concurrent local dispatches during cold (`is_cold()` check), logs `local_dispatch_denied ... cold_start=True`.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `provider_cooldown_seconds: 60` (line 581).

## Desired change

- In `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` and `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()`, check `cold_start.is_cold(config)`. If cold and the error is HTTP 503 or a connection error, **do not** call `mark_provider_unavailable()` or bump the failure counter. Instead, defer the request (return Retry-After using `cold_start.retry_after_seconds(config)`), and set an appropriate fallback reason.
- The deferred request should behave like a `Retry-After` signal to the caller (existing mechanism already supports this).
- A non-503 HTTP error (e.g., 500, 502) during the window should still call `mark_provider_unavailable()` to avoid masking genuine faults.
- A non-connection error during the window still quarantines normally.

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/cold_start.py` — read `is_cold()`, `retry_after_seconds()` for immunity decision.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown()` (~4871), `_handle_connection_error_in_fallback()` (~4832), `mark_provider_unavailable()` (~2141).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — cold-start dispatch gating (line ~1086) — verify no interaction conflicts.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `note_model_loaded()` call sites (~230, ~2007, ~2042, ~2222) — confirm window is armed before first 503s.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — cold-start config knobs.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission test suite; add the grace-period immunity cases here (or a sibling test module).
- `proxy/README.md` — update cooldown/cold-start documentation.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR01SJBP005I0OR** — "Fallback not recovering after model-loading 503; returns all providers exhausted" (completed). Sibling investigation.
- **LP-0MUCEEZ6B003NZH5** — "Restart-resilient local dispatch: prevent post-restart pool wedge from no-progress prefills" (completed). Parent epic / adjacent.
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** — "proxyctl: restart command" (completed). Restart tooling context.
- **LP-0MRE4NBQ5009V5BX** — "Add dual-threshold large-context routing bypass (cold-cache + warm-cache)" (completed). Cold/warm routing interaction.
- **LP-0MUYN2RD800889S2** — "[test-failure] tests/test_cold_start_admission.py::test_proxy_to_local_warm_bypasses_cold_cap — failing test" (completed). Existing cold-start admission test suite.

### Investigation context
- **LP-0MV9UNE75004903J** — mode-flip frequency investigation (restart-frequency context).
- **LP-0MV9UNKVK007TN7E** — proxy restart frequency examination (restart causes).

### Repository references
- `proxy/README.md` — cold-start / cooldown documentation surface.
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_admission.py` — existing cold-start admission tests (extend for immunity cases).

## Appendix

- Q: Where should the immunity window anchor? — Answer (Map): Reuse `cold_start.is_cold()` as the single immunity-boundary signal (recommended option a).
- Q: Scope of deferred failures during the window? — Answer (Map): Strictly HTTP 503 + connection errors; all other 5xx still quarantine (recommended option a).


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-16T12:39Z (plan skill, herdr-downtime dispatch): decomposed parent into 3 test-first children:
  - LP-0MVAYO1ZM005ZWTF (task, tests) — grace-period immunity tests (red repro + post-fix verification; parent ACs 1-4).
  - LP-0MVAYO1GD002CDVJ (feature, implementation) — deferral branch in provider error handlers; depends on tests.
  - LP-0MVAYO2HB00899L0 (docs) — config knobs, code comments, README/routing docs, post-change evidence; parent ACs 6-7; depends on implementation.
  - Dep edges: Implementation → Tests; Docs → Implementation (test-first ordering).
  - AC coverage review (tree_coverage): 100% covered, parent sub-ACs (a)-(e) all matched; recommendation 'proceed'; stage advanced to plan_complete.
  - Effort/risk re-estimated via effort-and-risk skill: Small / Medium (score 9).
  - No new open questions this session; the parent Appendix (Q1/Q2) already resolved the two key design decisions.

## Problem

Pi displays the proxy's `X-Resolved-Model` response header as the model string. That header is built as `<provider>/<model>` in two places:

- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` `_resolved_model_header` (LP-0MR4ZIGDT004A3E1)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` `_build_resolved_model_value` / `_add_resolved_model_header`

Both prefer the config `provider` brand field and only fall back to the entry `name` when `provider` is absent. As a result, the free-tier entry `munitoai-free` (and its paid sibling `munitoai`, which share `provider: MunitoAI` and `model: deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`) both report `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. The "free" marker exists only in the entry `name`, the `api_key_env` (`MUNITOAI_FREE_API_KEY`), and the auth.json key stem (`munitoai_free`) — none of which enter the display path (introduced by LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO, "use actual provider name, not provider entry name").

Operators therefore cannot tell free-tier from paid-tier service in Pi, and requests appear to "bypass" the free tier even when they are served by it.

## Goal

Make the `X-Resolved-Model` header (and any equivalent chunk/display path) distinguish provider **tiers** (free vs paid) without losing the provider-brand attribution added in LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO. Design target: a tier-aware display — e.g. the free MunitoAI entry resolves to a string containing `free` (such as `MunitoAI Free/...`) while the paid entry keeps its paid label — without touching failure-domain, cooldown, or usage-limit quarantine keys (which key on entry name / API-key account and must stay unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A request served by `munitoai-free` returns an `X-Resolved-Model` header whose human-readable provider component conveys the `free` tier (e.g. `MunitoAI Free/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` or a tier-carrying equivalent), while `munitoai` (paid) returns the paid label.
- AC2: The two MunitoAI entries produce **distinct** `X-Resolved-Model` strings; free and paid are no longer byte-identical.
- AC3: `_build_resolved_model_value` (provider.py) and `_resolved_model_header` (proxy_remote.py) share the same tier-resolution logic via a single helper (a new config field such as `display_name`, or a rule that includes the entry `name` when it encodes a tier). No duplicated or divergent logic between the two sites.
- AC4: Failure-domain keys, entry cooldown keys, brand cooldown keys, usage-limit account keys, and `X-Provider` header values are **unchanged** — the change is display-only.
- AC5: Config option preferred over code special-casing "MunitoAI": the change must not hard-code provider names or `free` detection in Python; it must work for any entry via config.
- AC6: Tests: existing `proxy/tests/test_resolved_model_header.py` still passes; new/adjusted tests assert (a) free entry emits the tier-carrying display string, (b) paid entry emits its distinct string, (c) headers for local providers (`local/<model>`) are unchanged, (d) failure-domain/cooldown keys unaffected.

## References

- LP-0MR4ZIGDT004A3E1 — Show the model being used in Pi (origin of X-Resolved-Model)
- LP-0MRC4G7ZL005L1BO — Fix X-Resolved-Model header format: use actual provider name, not provider entry name (the behaviour this item refines)
- LP-0MV5UPXKL002MSKB / LP-0MV6ENYYH006XX0Z — MunitoAI provider additions / tier placement
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVCBMERY004SHCK** – Commit pending MunitoAI free/paid provider reorder (config.yaml/config-fast.yaml + fixtures + fallback-chain test) (completed)
